{{Short description|Austrian physicist (1905–1961)}}
'''Felix Issidorowitsch Frankl''' (12 March 1905, [[Vienna]] – 7 Aprile 1961, [[Nalchik]] {{langx|ru|Феликс Исидорович Франкль}}) was an Austrian mathematician, who went to live in the [[Soviet Union]] where he had an academic career as a university professor.<ref name="mil encyc">{{cite web |title=Франкль Феликс Исидорович |url=http://encyclopedia.mil.ru/encyclopedia/dictionary/details_rvsn.htm?id=14020@morfDictionary |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210509194228/http://encyclopedia.mil.ru/encyclopedia/dictionary/details_rvsn.htm?id=14020@morfDictionary |archive-date=2021-05-09 |access-date=9 May 2021 |website=Военный энциклопедический словарь |publisher=[[Ministry of Defence of the Russian Federation]] |language=ru}}</ref>

He studied topology at the Faculty of Mathematics of the [[University of Vienna]] under [[Hans Hahn (mathematician)|Hans Hahn]], gaining his doctorate in 1927.<ref name="FIF">{{cite web |date=16 March 2015 |title=Франкль Феликс Исидорович |url=http://library.ruslan.cc/authors/%D1%84%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%BA%D0%BB%D1%8C-%D1%84%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D1%81-%D0%B8%D1%81%D0%B8%D0%B4%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190402222009/http://library.ruslan.cc/authors/%D1%84%D1%80%D0%B0%D0%BD%D0%BA%D0%BB%D1%8C-%D1%84%D0%B5%D0%BB%D0%B8%D0%BA%D1%81-%D0%B8%D1%81%D0%B8%D0%B4%D0%BE%D1%80%D0%BE%D0%B2%D0%B8%D1%87/ |archive-date=2 April 2019 |access-date=9 May 2021 |website=Научное Наследие России |publisher=[[:ru:Научное Наследие России]] |language=ru}}</ref>

Frankl joined the Austrian Communist Party in 1928 and (with the assistance of [[Pavel Aleksandrov]]) emigrated to the Soviet Union in 1929.<ref name='zusmanovich'>Pasha Zusmanovich, "Mathematicians Going East," Journal of Humanistic Mathematics, Volume 14 Issue
1 (January 2024), pages 114-167. DOI: 10.5642/jhummath.EGCM7534. Available at: https://scholarship.claremont.edu/jhm/vol14/iss1/8. Pages 121-22.</ref> Here he initially collaborated with [[Lev Pontryagin]] in topology (they a paper co-authored a paper published in 1930 in the ''[[Mathematische Annalen]]''. His interests then shifted to certain particular differential equations which are important for high-speed aerodynamics. These differential equations were of mixed elliptic-hyperbolic type. They determined the transition in aerodynamics between transonic and supersonic speeds.

He attended the [[First International Topological Conference]] held in [[Moscow]] in 1935.<ref name="ANS">{{cite journal |last1=Apushkinskaya |first1=Darya E. |last2=Nazarov |first2=Alexander I. |last3=Sinkevich |first3=Galina I. |title=In Search of Shadows: The First Topological Conference, Moscow 1935 |journal=The Mathematical Intelligencer |date=December 2019 |volume=41 |issue=4 |pages=37–42 |doi=10.1007/s00283-019-09907-6|arxiv=1903.02065 |s2cid=119170777 }}</ref> In 1957 he was awarded the [[Leonhard Euler Gold Medal]] of the [[Russian Academy of Sciences]].<ref name="mil encyc"/>

In 1950 he was expelled from the communist party and exiled to [[Bishkek]].<ref name='zusmanovich' /> He died in 1961 in [[Nalchik]].<ref name='zusmanovich' />
